extraction.name: RoboFAC dataset
extraction.description: The RoboFAC dataset is a large-scale and diverse dataset for question-answering on robot failure videos. It comprises 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. The dataset encompasses robotic tasks of varying complexity, ranging from simple short-horizon tasks to complex long-horizon tasks, and tasks executed in dynamic environments. It includes 14 simulated tasks and 6 real-world tasks, with two of the real-world tasks not present in the simulation environment. The dataset includes six types of failures, spanning three hierarchical levels of error. Variations in backgrounds and camera viewpoints are introduced to enhance visual diversity and facilitate the development of models with better visual generalization capabilities. It includes 8,960 failure trajectories in simulation and 480 in the real world, along with 1,160 successful trajectories from simulation and 122 from real-world executions to prevent overfitting.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao
extraction.publisher: School of AI, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The RoboFAC dataset was constructed through a pipeline involving both simulation and real-world data collection. Simulation data for 14 robotic tasks was collected in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. For each custom task, an expert policy was defined, and erroneous trajectories were generated by replacing parts of the expert policy with code snippets at selected substages to intentionally cause robotic task failures. Real-world data for 6 tasks (including two unique to real-world) was collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. Each recorded robotic failure video was accompanied by a descriptive text detailing the substage where the failure occurred, the taxonomy of failure, a detailed textual explanation of the error, and the perturbed pose if applicable. Both failure and successful trajectories were collected.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Simulation data was collected from the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Real-world data was collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To generate failure data in the simulation environment, the original expert policy was replaced with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at a selected substage, intentionally causing the overall robotic task to fail.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: After initial data collection, thorough manual data cleaning was performed to ensure that motion planning trajectories aligned with their corresponding textual descriptions. Approximately 75% of the collected data was retained after this cleaning process.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw data was annotated to create video-based QA samples for eight distinct question types, covering Task Understanding, Failure Analysis, and Failure Correction. For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from the textual descriptions associated with the videos. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction), GPT-4o was used to generate reference answers, taking both the video and its textual description as input, guided by a specific prompt provided in Appendix C.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To ensure annotation quality, all outputs from GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: The dataset includes 78K video QA samples, corresponding to eight distinct question types.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include the current non-seamless integration of the RoboFAC model's correction suggestions into VLA-controlled robotic systems. The VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions also presents a challenge for further enhancement.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for training and evaluating multimodal models for robotic failure video understanding. Specifically, 60K QA pairs from the simulated dataset are used as the training set, while 10K simulated QA pairs and 8K real-world QA pairs are used for evaluation (testing).
